tool_contract.note: partial by tool NAME only: 5 production assistant tools are exposed; schemas and result shapes are production verbatim

function.description: Search the app's LOCAL INDEX of scanned messages (all folders it has seen, newest first). Instant; covers the window the app has processed. For older mail or other folders use search_mail.
function.name: search_messages

query.description: free text; matches sender, subject and snippet

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD; only messages seen on/after this date

until.description: YYYY-MM-DD; only messages seen on/before this date

function.description: Read one message: headers plus the full text body. Identify it with message_id (from search_messages) OR folder + uid (from search_mail).
function.name: read_message

function.description: Move one message to a folder (created if missing). Identify it with message_id OR folder + uid. Moves never delete mail.
function.name: move_message

function.description: List the user's current filter rules in order: id, name, enabled, conditions, actions. Call this BEFORE proposing a rule so you can update an existing rule rather than stacking a near-duplicate.
function.name: list_rules

function.description: Propose a filter rule for the user to approve with one click. Approved rules sort matching mail automatically (top to bottom, first match wins). A rule with NO actions is a GUARD: matching mail stays put and nothing else (later rules, LLM filing) can move it.
function.name: propose_rule

actions.description: what the rule does; OMIT (or {"keep": true}) for a guard rule that keeps matching mail in place and stops further rules

plugin.description: op=plugin only: a matcher plugin id (mt-cjk-matcher checks for CJK text); the plugin decides by its own logic

placement.description: where the rule lands in the list; use "top" for guard/protection rules so they catch mail before other rules act (default bottom)

updates_rule_id.description: id of an EXISTING rule this proposal changes (from list_rules). Set it when the user asks to change/adjust a rule instead of creating a near-duplicate; the proposal then replaces that rule's name/conditions/actions
